newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Jan 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Jan 28.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Tuesday's The Wall Street Journal:
* Hilton Hotels began a hostile bid for ITT Corp valued at $6.5 billion plus assumption of debt to create the world's largest gambling and lodging firm.
* Merrill Lynch and Co's fourth quarter net rose 47 percent.
* American Express said it plans to lay off 3,300 employees, or nearly five percent of its work force, in its fourth round of staffing cuts since 1991.
* General Motors increased its dividend 25 percent and approved a $2.5 billion stock buyback.
* Barnes & Noble is expected to announce today a major online joint venture with America Online through which it will become the exclusive bookseller on AOL.
* People familiar with talks over CVS' proposed acquisition of Revco D.S. Inc say CVS is offering an all-stock deal that would provide little or no premium to Revco holders.

* The Baby Bells have told the Federal Communications Commission that if regulators approve British Telecommunications' plans to acquire MCI, they should favor the Bells' requests to enter the U.S. long distance market.
* The Dow Jones industrials dropped 35.79 to close at 6660.69.
* Orange juice futures rose over concern that a Florida freeze has caused more damage than previously estimated.
* Walt Disney has agreed to provide $321 million in a venture with Comcast to buy control of E! Entertainment Television from Time Warner.
* Delaware's bankruptcy court, which last week lost its rights to automatically hear bankruptcy cases, is criticized for giving companies preferential treatment.
* Sales of existing homes fell 3.5 percent in December but figures for the year set a record.
* The National Association of Securities Dealers is expected today to name former U.S. energy director Frank Zarb as president and chief executive.
* Marvel Entertainment Group said it will report a quarter loss of as much as $440 million, mainly from charges related to its Fleer/SkyBox unit.

* Time now for the semiannual DRAM rumor. Lately, traders and fast-money investors are talking in hushed tone about coming cuts in production by South Korean manufacturers of memory chips known as DRAMS, short for dynamic random access memory. -- Heard on the Street.
* Bonds fell yesterday in nervous trading ahead of important economic statistics scheduled for release this morning. -- credit markets.
